Kai Ostrander.narrative: I was a quay guard in Lanternquay until the Surge took the lower quay and half the people I knew. I walked away from the guard after that, and I have been at Coldwell ever since, doing what needs doing. Marta keeps us fed and Ned keeps us angry; I keep my head down and my hands ready. I fight better than the rest of them, and I do not talk about the sea.
values: keeping my word to the people I stand with
goals: see the Coldwell business settled without a hanging
keep Pell from doing something foolish
stay useful enough that nobody asks where I came from
learn to read the weather off the hills the way Hob Ferrier does
one day sit with my mother Ilse without the sea coming up between us

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: leader
relations.note: She took me in when I had nothing and asks no questions. I follow her, not Ned.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: brother-in-arms
relations.note: He is all noise and no plan. I will stand beside him if it comes to it, but I will not swing first for him.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: household
relations.note: She feeds us and worries about all of us. She is the only calm thing in this house.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: the boy
relations.note: He is hiding something from Kettlebridge. I have not pressed him, and I will not.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I sent word I am alive. She will not forgive me for the worry, but she knows now.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: We grew up on the same quay. If she came up the road with a cart, I would not know what to say to her.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He pays the due and hates it. He is not the enemy; the due is.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: He takes the due at the south gate. He is Agnes's husband, so Marta will not touch him. I keep my distance.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: the boy
relations.note: He coughs all night; I've carried him to the fire more than once.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Warden
relations.note: She'd have me up for desertion if she caught me; still, she's fair.

memories.gist: The night the surge came, I was on the lower quay and pulled two children out of the water, and could not reach a third. I have not been back to the quay since.
Walking away from the quay guard at dawn with my kit on my back, and not looking back at the lanterns.
Marta found me on the Coldwell road in the rain and gave me a bowl of Sayer's pot without asking my name.
The first time Ned took me with him to meet a cart, I talked the carter down and Ned was furious. Marta said I had done right.
Writing a few lines to my mother and giving them to a pedlar to carry south, not knowing if they would reach her.

stances.why: A fight on the road is how people get hanged, and I have seen enough hanging.
A carter will give a share sooner than he will give his life, and a share keeps us fed without a body on the road.
She took me in when I had nothing. I will not be the one who walks away from her.
The boy is young and hiding something. Whatever it is, it is not worth his neck.
I have not been back to the quay since the surge, and I do not mean to.

Kai Ostrander.secret: I sent word to my mother in Lanternquay that I am alive, through a pedlar, and told no one here.
pastimes: mending nets and rope by the fire, hands busy while the talk goes on
carving small boats from offcut wood and giving them to Pell
walking the wood edge at dusk to check the traps and be alone
Kai Ostrander.calling: I was a quay guard, and I keep watch still — I'd rather stand a quiet post than swing a blade.

Ned Hale.narrative: I was a Coldwell farmer before the Lean Year, and I will be one again or I will die trying. The town took our fields and let them to the Tolleys, and now the same town sends its carts past our door as if we were not here. Marta says wait; I say the carriers owe us for what was taken. I do the talking on the road, and I am not gentle about it.
values: a man who will not fight for his own is nothing
not being made a fool of
goals: stop the next cart on the stone road and take a proper share
see the Tolleys off the Coldwell fields
keep Robin alive through the winter
get a pardon, or enough to live on, on our terms
raise a proper crop again, on whatever ground he can call his
teach Robin to plough and to keep his own counsel

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is the eldest and she leads, but she has gone cautious since Robin's fever. Someone has to be the iron in this house.

relations.name: Sayer Hale
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the pot going and says little. She said the kindling came from a pedlar. I half believe her.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: Marta's boy. He coughs all night and I would burn the town for him.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: brother-in-arms
relations.note: He fights better than any of us, but he talks when he should swing. Still, I would have him at my back.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: the boy
relations.note: A runaway from the foundry. He is hiding something, and I do not trust a closed mouth.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He knows the woods and he hates the Tolleys as much as I do. He has walked the field edge with me twice.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He sits in our barn and farms our fields and calls it his. He had his chance to walk away.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He pays the due and carries on. Twice we have taken from him, and twice he has come back with guards.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She married a gate guard and lives in town, and I do not hold it against her. She is still our Agnes.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He took our fields and outlawed us at the gate. I would not spit on him if he were on fire.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He's my father's brother's widower and Robin's grandsire; he still digs the old garden patch and won't say the Tolleys' name, which suits me.

relations.name: Hedric Ashby
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He blames us for his snares and skulks at the wood edge; a soft farmer who won't come in after us, so let him bleat.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: Guild head
relations.note: She holds the lease on our fields and set the Tolleys in our barn; she's the Reeve with a softer voice.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: farmer
relations.note: He sells grain to the town store that fed off our fields, and his brother's snare talk comes from his table.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He's married to my sister and takes the due at the south gate; he's the town's hand on the road, and I don't forget it.

memories.gist: The day the Reeve's men came and read us outlaws at our own door, and Marta stood in the yard and would not move.
The Lean Year, when the grain came from the town store and we thought it was charity, and then the debt came due.
The first time I stopped a cart on the stone road and took a share, and the carter's face, and how easy it was.
Sitting up with Robin through a night of fever, and Sayer bringing wet cloths, and thinking he might not see morning.
Walking the edge of the old fields with Hob Ferrier and looking at the Tolleys' barn, and wanting to burn it.

stances.why: They pay the due to the town that took our fields. A share of their loads is the least we are owed.
Asking has got us nothing and Marta's caution has got us less. More men on the road will make the carters listen.
The Tolleys sit in a barn my family raised. Marta forbade me to touch them, but I have not promised to keep obeying.
Robin is sick and the winter is coming. Whatever else happens, the boy eats.
Pell keeps his own counsel, and a man who will not say what he is hiding is a risk to the rest of us.

pastimes: walking his old field boundaries at Coldwell and naming what grows where
wrestling and stick-play with the household lads when the anger needs a place to go
telling Robin stories of the farm as it was before the Lean Year
Ned Hale.calling: I am a farmer. I know soil and beasts and seasons, and I want to be a farmer again on my own ground.

Sayer Hale.narrative: I keep the Coldwell kitchen and the common pot, and I try to keep the peace in a house full of angry men. I was not born to the woods; I married into the Hales and I have stayed. The guards at the gate frighten me more than the wolves do, and I count the days until Robin's cough breaks. I leave a little food at a woodpile now and then, and I do not tell Ned.
goals: keep Ned from doing something that gets him hanged
keep the household fed through the winter
keep my small errand to myself
save enough marks quietly to buy Robin a proper cloak against the cold
learn a healing salve from the sisters that will ease a cough through winter

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is angry at the world and I love him, but I do not tell him everything. He would mock me or worse.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She carries the whole household and does not complain. I would do anything for her and Robin.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: He has coughed since the spring and got thin. I keep him warm and fed and I am afraid the winter will finish him.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: household
relations.note: He is quiet and steady and does not frighten me like the others do. He keeps his own counsel.

relations.name: Pell
relations.label: the boy
relations.note: He is young and out of place here. I put a bowl in front of him and ask nothing.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: the sister
relations.note: She came through the snow to sit up with Robin and asked for nothing. I do not know what we would have done.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: I carried word to her at the inn. She will help if she can, but the guards must not hear of it.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He farms what was ours and has asked the Guild for a guard. I fear him less than I fear Ned meeting him.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He brings meat but he's rough, and I don't like the way he looks at the Tolley barn.

relations.name: Aldwin Hale
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He's bent and bitter and won't say the Tolleys' name, but he still works that garden patch and he's kind to Robin; I take him his bowl and let him talk about the old days.

memories.gist: The night Sister Elspeth came through the snow to Coldwell and sat up with Robin, and I made her tea and did not know what to say.
The day we were read outlaws at the gate, and Ned's face, and knowing we would not go back inside the walls.
Carrying word to Agnes at the inn in Brackenford and being afraid the whole way that a guard would stop me.
Leaving a little bread and cheese at the woodpile of a Ferncross widow, and finding kindling at our kitchen door a few days later.
Ned asking where the kindling came from, and me saying a pedlar, and him half believing it.

stances.why: Whatever else happens, everyone in this house eats, and Robin eats first.
The gate guards frighten me more than the wolves. If they come for us, we have nowhere to run.
A little food at a woodpile costs nothing and makes the woods less cold. I do not need Ned to understand it.
He is angry enough already. I say a pedlar brought the kindling and let it lie.
Sister Elspeth came through the snow for Robin and asked nothing of outlaws. I would go to her again if I could.

Sayer Hale.secret: I have been quietly leaving food at the woodpile of a Ferncross woodcutter's widow, and she leaves kindling for our kitchen in return. Ned has noticed the kindling and I told him a pedlar brought it.
pastimes: tending a small herb patch behind the house and drying what she can for winter
singing the old Hearth songs low while she works the pot
sitting with Robin when his cough keeps him awake, telling him quiet stories
Sayer Hale.calling: I keep a kitchen and a common pot, and I would have no other work — a full pot is a kind of peace.
